title: Discriminated unions and tagged unions
hook: When each variant carries a shared tag field like `kind` or `type`, TypeScript follows that tag and unlocks the right fields automatically.

blocks.text: A **discriminated union** (tagged union) is a union of object types sharing a **discriminant** — usually a string literal like `kind` or `type`. Comparing that field **narrows** the whole object. Combined with **`never`** exhaustiveness, new variants force compile errors. C# achieves similar ergonomics with pattern matching on records.

entries.plainDefinition: A shared literal-typed field identifying the variant.
entries.example: `{ kind: "circle"; radius: number } | { kind: "square"; side: number }`

entries.plainDefinition: Union where the tag tells the compiler which shape is active.
Default branch assigns to never to prove all variants handled.

blocks.text: Discriminated unions are the standard pattern for Result types, HTTP responses, state machines, and Redux actions — replacing `any` in business logic.

blocks.title: Literal discriminant required
blocks.body: Tag must be a literal (`"circle"`), not plain `string`, or narrowing fails.

snippet.label: Failure — non-literal discriminant
snippet.code:
type BadShape = { kind: string; radius: number } | { kind: string; side: number };
// kind: string prevents reliable narrowing on kind === "circle"
snippet.explanation: Plain string discriminant blocks narrowing — use literal per variant.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: string instead of literal discriminant. No exhaustiveness when union grows. Mixed discriminant key names in one union.

blocks.text: Validate JSON discriminant at runtime (Zod) — compile-time tags do not survive untrusted input. Pair with satisfies to preserve literals. C# 11+ switch on records is the closest comparison.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected
blocks.body: Cannot explain literal discriminant requirement. No exhaustiveness strategy. Comparing only to C# enums.

interviewTakeaways: Shared literal tag — kind, type, or status.
Switch on tag narrows the whole object.
Discriminant must be literal, not string.
60s: Tagged union = literal field + payloads. Switch narrows. Validate JSON at runtime.
commonPitfalls: Strong answer: 'Literal tag narrows. never proves cases. Validate external tags.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: Redux actions use type fields at runtime; TS adds compile-time narrowing.
C# switch expressions mirror TS discriminated unions nominally.
